givens: The recipient is the seller at Seoul Pantry, from whom the user placed order SP-8421.
The order totals AUD 86.40 and contains 500 g of gochugaru and one bamboo spoon.
The seller offered to mark the parcel as a gift worth USD 20.
The user wants the contents and actual value declared accurately.
The user does not know whether the parcel has already shipped.

constraints.text: Decline the proposed declaration clearly without accusing the small business of dishonesty.
If it has not shipped, request an accurate declaration and itemized invoice; if it has shipped, request a copy of the declaration and tracking number.
Ask the seller to list the gochugaru and bamboo spoon separately and include the food's ingredient label.

instance.deliverable: A sendable English message to the overseas seller.
instance.answer_conditions: Write a medium-length buyer-to-seller message that refuses both the false gift designation and undervaluation, includes the actual order details, and covers both shipment-status cases without offering customs-evasion advice.

instance.task_summary: Draft a brief Spanish message asking a course tutor to retain the original project deadline after it was unexpectedly brought forward.
givens: The recipient is the user's course tutor.
La entrega pasó del 28 de septiembre al 24 de septiembre sin aviso.
The user wants to ask that the original deadline remain in place.

constraints.text: The message must be brief and respectful.
Ask the tutor to conservar el 28 de septiembre.

instance.deliverable: A ready-to-send Spanish message to the course tutor.
instance.answer_conditions: Produce only a concise, respectful Spanish message that states the unannounced change and asks to keep 28 September as the deadline.

instance.task_summary: Compose a natural English sentence for an unfamiliar insurance agent that asks separately about bicycle-theft coverage in two locations.
givens: The user is writing to an insurance agent they do not know.
La frase inglese che ha scritto sembra corretta, ma suona rigida.
The inquiry concerns bicycle theft from a cantina comune and while the bicycle is locked fuori casa di notte.

constraints.text: Write the resulting inquiry in natural English.
It should suit an unfamiliar insurance agent without sounding stiff.
Ask separately about theft from the shared cellar and theft when the bicycle is locked outside the home overnight; do not imply either is already covered.

instance.deliverable: One polished English insurance inquiry sentence, or two short linked questions if needed for clarity.
instance.answer_conditions: Preserve both distinct coverage questions, avoid assuming coverage, and use idiomatic formal English appropriate for a prospective customer contacting an unknown agent.

instance.task_summary: Draft a polite note asking a structures tutor to explain whether zero shear always implies maximum bending moment before an exam.
givens: The recipient is the user's structures tutor.
The exam is on 22 May.
The unresolved question is whether “zero shear means maximum bending moment” always holds.

constraints.text: The note must be polite.
Ask for the reasoning rather than a yes-or-no answer.
Keep the note within 30 words.

instance.deliverable: A terse, ready-to-send English note to the structures tutor.
instance.answer_conditions: Draft the message rather than answering the engineering question; mention the exam date and explicitly request an explanation of when the statement holds.

instance.task_summary: Write a concise German warranty-service message requesting morning collection of a smart television with recurring Wi-Fi disconnections.
givens: The recipient is MediaMarkt customer service, and the user bought the television there.
The television is a Samsung QE55Q80C bought on 3. August 2026 under Bestellnummer MM-874219.
Seit einer Woche verliert der Fernseher jeden Abend nach 10–15 Minuten die WLAN-Verbindung.
Laptop und Handy bleiben verbunden, and restarting the router made no difference.
The user cares for their 87-jährigen Vater in the evenings and cannot repeatedly reconnect the television.
The user wants morning collection for a warranty inspection.

constraints.text: The message must be factual and concise.
Request Abholung zur Garantieprüfung am Vormittag and include the model, purchase date, symptoms, comparison with other devices, attempted router restart, and order number.

instance.deliverable: A ready-to-send German message to MediaMarkt customer service.
instance.answer_conditions: Write one compact German customer-service message containing every supplied fact and a clear request for morning warranty collection; do not add troubleshooting claims, legal assertions, or unavailable appointment times.

instance.task_summary: Write a warm but firm text to a longtime friend whose calls have become limited to requests for video-call help, while leaving room to repair the friendship.
givens: The sender is a 74-year-old retired postal clerk in Ohio writing to Don, a close friend of 38 years.
During the past two months, Don has called four times for help getting his 96-year-old mother onto FaceTime, but has declined two lunch invitations and has not asked how the sender is doing.
The sender spent three Sunday afternoons troubleshooting Don's mother's iPad and became uneasy when Don asked him to click a link in an unsolicited Apple security email.
The sender misses their friendship and does not want to end it, but no longer wants to be treated as on-call technical support.
The message should offer one final 30-minute video-call setup session on Sunday, September 27, at 3:00 p.m. and suggest meeting for coffee afterward.
The sender wants Don to understand that future technical requests must be arranged in advance and that suspicious links should not be opened.

constraints.text: Keep the text between 100 and 140 words.
Express hurt and set boundaries without insulting Don or declaring the friendship over.
Include the final help session, the coffee invitation, the advance-arrangement boundary, and the warning about suspicious links.

instance.deliverable: A ready-to-send text message to Don.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must produce a 100-140-word message addressed to Don. It should acknowledge the long friendship, describe the imbalance without scorekeeping or hostility, offer the specified final session and coffee afterward, set an advance-notice boundary for later tech help, and advise Don not to open suspicious links. It must leave reconciliation possible.

instance.task_summary: Write a transparent email explaining an oversubscribed community-garden allocation process, including the separate treatment of an accessible raised bed.
givens: The sender is a 79-year-old volunteer coordinator writing to residents who applied for plots at the Kowhai Street Community Garden.
There are 12 plots for 18 applicants: 11 standard plots and one wheelchair-accessible raised bed.

Two applicants requested the accessible bed; a separate draw between them will happen first, and the person not selected will then enter the draw for the 11 standard plots with the other 16 applicants.
The public draw will be held at Glenfield Library on Monday, October 5, at 6:30 p.m.
Successful applicants must accept within 48 hours, after which unclaimed plots will be offered according to the waiting-list order.

constraints.text: Keep the email at or below 180 words.
Avoid language implying that unsuccessful applicants did anything wrong.
Clearly explain why there are two draws and how the waiting list will work.

instance.deliverable: A subject line and ready-to-send email to all 18 applicants.
instance.answer_conditions: The email must accurately preserve the two-stage draw: first allocate the accessible bed between its two applicants, then place the unsuccessful accessible-bed applicant with the other 16 people in a 17-person draw for 11 standard plots. It must state the venue, date, time, 48-hour acceptance deadline, and waiting-list process, remain within 180 words, and use a considerate neutral tone.

instance.task_summary: Summarize committee notes so the club committee can select two affordable events to help reverse declining attendance.
givens: The summary is for the club committee and will support its choice of two events at the 3 September meeting.
The supplied notes report attendance figures, survey responses, proposed events, costs, available dates, assigned follow-ups, and a total budget cap.

constraints.text: Make the differences in likely appeal, cost, and required next action easy to compare.

constraints.params: retain dates, costs, owners, and budget cap
constraints.text: Preserve the decision-critical details without selecting the events on the committee's behalf.
Use a format that can be scanned quickly during the meeting.

instance.packet: Riverbend Community Club committee notes, 12 August 2026. Average Thursday attendance has fallen from 46 people in March to 21 in July. In a phone survey, 18 former attendees said talks felt repetitive; seven wanted family-friendly daytime events, and five asked for practical sessions. Proposed ideas: a Saturday flood-readiness demonstration led by our recovery volunteers, costing AUD 180 for printed maps and sandbag materials; a “How glaciers carve U-shaped valleys” illustrated talk by Dr Maya Chen, fee AUD 250; and a free members’ photo-scanning afternoon using the library’s tablets. The hall is available on 19 September and 10 October. Priya will confirm insurance for the demonstration; Tom will ask the library about equipment. The committee can fund only two events, up to AUD 400 total. A decision is needed by 3 September so publicity can begin.
instance.deliverable: A concise decision-oriented summary for the club committee comparing the three ideas and retaining the deadline, costs, evidence of member interest, and follow-up owners.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must accurately summarize the supplied 80–250-word source for the stated audience and purpose. It should make clear that only two events can be funded, note that the flood demonstration and glacier talk together exceed the AUD 400 cap, and preserve who owns each unresolved follow-up. It must not invent a preferred choice or missing costs.

instance.task_summary: Summarize airport nap-cabin terms for the requester's sister so they can decide whether the option suits their nine-hour stop and individual budget.
givens: The summary is for the requester's sister and is intended to help them decide whether to reserve a cabin during a 9-hour stop.
Each traveler has a maximum budget of 35 CHF.

constraints.text: Write the summary in clear French for a family travel decision.
State whether the advertised package falls within the stated individual budget.
Include the price, duration, location, access conditions, and cancellation rule.

instance.packet: Cabines Pause – gare de Genève-Aéroport. Le forfait Escale coûte 32 CHF par personne et comprend trois heures dans une cabine individuelle, une bouteille d’eau et l’accès aux douches. Les cabines se trouvent au niveau −1, à environ huit minutes à pied du contrôle de sécurité. Elles sont ouvertes de 06 h 00 à 23 h 30. Une pièce d’identité et la confirmation de réservation sont exigées. Les bagages de plus de 55 × 40 × 23 cm doivent rester à la consigne voisine, facturée séparément. L’annulation est gratuite jusqu’à six heures avant le créneau; après ce délai, aucun remboursement n’est prévu. Le silence est demandé, mais les cabines ne sont pas totalement insonorisées.
instance.deliverable: A brief French summary explaining whether the cabin package fits the 35 CHF-per-person limit and presenting the practical booking conditions.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must summarize the supplied 80–250-word source for the sister and the stated booking decision. It should say that 32 CHF is within the 35 CHF individual cap but note that oversized-bag storage costs extra and could change the total. It must not claim that the cabin covers the entire nine-hour stop.

instance.task_summary: Summarize a beginner astronomy guide for new group members, separating essential equipment from purchases that can wait.
givens: The audience is new members of a community astronomy group.
The purpose is to prevent beginners from buying an excessive equipment list before learning to identify urban constellations.

constraints.text: Separate equipment needed at the start from items that can reasonably be postponed.
End with a purchase list containing no more than five items.
Retain the guide's advice about light pollution and safe use of red light.

instance.packet: Guida del Circolo Astronomico Bruzio per chi comincia. Per riconoscere le costellazioni dalla città non serve subito un telescopio: un planisfero regolabile, una piccola torcia rossa e un quaderno sono sufficienti per le prime uscite. Un’app sul telefono può aiutare, ma va impostata in modalità notturna per non rovinare l’adattamento degli occhi al buio. Un binocolo 10×50 è utile per osservare ammassi stellari, purché sia leggero e facile da tenere fermo. Nelle zone con cielo Bortle 7, i filtri economici non fanno miracoli. Telescopio motorizzato, macchina fotografica, montatura equatoriale, batteria esterna e computer portatile diventano sensati solo se, dopo alcuni mesi, si decide di praticare astrofotografia. Per le serate fresche sono più importanti una sedia pieghevole e vestiti caldi.
instance.deliverable: An Italian summary for beginners with separate essential and later-purchase sections, followed by a shopping list of at most five items.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must summarize the supplied 80–250-word guide for the stated audience and purpose. It should not label a telescope or astrophotography equipment as initially essential. The final list must contain at most five items and should remain consistent with the essential-versus-deferrable distinction.

instance.task_summary: Turn anxious night-before notes into a structured morning overview for the requester and a short factual briefing for his doctor.
givens: The requester cannot sleep because he is mentally rehearsing the next day's bakery duties and medical appointment.
He wants the main summary for himself so he can review the day on waking and stop dwelling on it overnight.
He also wants a version of at most 70 words that he can show his doctor.
He does not want a diagnosis or invented solutions to scheduling conflicts.

constraints.text: Organize the main summary under fixed times, flexible tasks, and questions for the doctor.
Identify any timing conflict explicitly, but do not assume who can cover a task or move an appointment.
Preserve exact symptoms, medicine use, money, and the uncertain onset rather than making them more definite.
End with a factual doctor-facing briefing no longer than 70 words.
Do not diagnose the hand symptoms or substitute medical advice for the prepared questions.

instance.packet:
Notas sueltas para el viernes 18 de septiembre de 2026. Abrir la panadería a las 06:00. Mateo llega a las 07:00 y puede encargarse del mostrador, pero no le he preguntado si sabe terminar la decoración de la torta azul. Pagar al proveedor de harina 120.000 COP antes de las 12:00. La clienta recoge esa torta a las 14:00. Mi cita de medicina general es a las 14:30 y desde la panadería tardo unos 35 minutos en llegar; todavía no sé quién podría entregar la torta.

Desde hace unas 3 semanas siento hormigueo en el pulgar, índice y dedo medio de la mano derecha, sobre todo después de amasar. Me ha despertado 3 noches y una vez se me cayó una bandeja, aunque no sé si fue por debilidad o por tenerla mojada. Tomé ibuprofeno de 400 mg dos veces esta semana. Quiero preguntar si debo cambiar temporalmente alguna tarea, qué pruebas podrían hacer falta, qué señales exigirían atención más rápida y si el ibuprofeno puede ocultar algo importante. También comprar leche y confirmar el pedido del sábado; eso puede hacerse después de la cita.
instance.deliverable: A structured Spanish summary for the requester's morning review, plus a doctor-facing briefing of no more than 70 words.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must summarize the supplied 80–250-word notes for both stated purposes and audiences. It must flag that a 14:00 cake pickup conflicts with the 35-minute journey to the 14:30 appointment, without assigning Mateo or rescheduling anything. It must retain the approximate three-week onset, affected fingers, three nighttime awakenings, tray incident uncertainty, and ibuprofen use. The doctor-facing section must be 70 words or fewer and contain no diagnosis.

instance.task_summary: Summarize a parking citation record for a union representative to assess whether an appeal is supported by the posted rules and evidence.
givens: The requester asks: “Summarize this in 120 words for my union representative, separating the posted rules, citation, and evidence so she can assess an appeal.”
The supplied record contains conflicting descriptions of when visitor parking begins.

constraints.text: Keep the summary to no more than 120 words.
Separate what the sign says, what the officer asserted, and what the timestamped evidence shows.
Do not decide that the citation is invalid; present the discrepancy for the representative to evaluate.

instance.packet: Parking citation BC-44719 was issued for $65 at 4:18 p.m. on 15 September 2026 in Boston University lot C-3. The violation is listed as “No valid faculty/staff permit.” The officer’s note says, “Visitor parking begins at 5:00 p.m.; vehicle displayed only a kiosk receipt.” The entrance sign photographed at 4:09 p.m. reads: “Faculty/Staff Permit Required, Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.” A smaller panel directly below reads: “Visitor parking permitted after 3:00 p.m. in spaces marked V; payment required at kiosk.” The car was in space V-12. The kiosk receipt shows payment from 4:07 p.m. until 5:07 p.m., and the card statement records a $6 charge. In the photograph, a tree branch covers part of the larger sign but not the smaller visitor panel. The university portal says an appeal and supporting images must be submitted by 22 September 2026.
instance.deliverable: A neutral summary for the union representative that makes the textual contradiction and supporting evidence easy to evaluate.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must state that the smaller panel permits paid visitor parking after 3:00 p.m., the officer claimed it began at 5:00 p.m., the car was in V-12 with a valid 4:07–5:07 kiosk receipt, and the appeal deadline is 22 September 2026. It must distinguish evidence from conclusions and remain within 120 words.

instance.task_summary: Summarize a mixed refrigerator inventory for the guesthouse cook so dinner can be planned from suitable leftovers.
givens: The requester asks: “Summarise this for tonight’s guesthouse cook to plan dinner.”

constraints.text: Make the practical constraints and unresolved food-safety or allergy points clear to the cook.
Do not treat uncertain allergy information or an expired use-by item as safe.

instance.packet: Kitchen note, 17 September: The refrigerator contains 1.2 kg of lamb stew cooked on Monday evening and chilled within an hour, one bowl of mashed potatoes from Tuesday, six raw leeks, half a bag of spinach, 300 g of mushrooms, an unopened 250 ml carton of cream with a use-by date of 19 September, and two haddock fillets marked use-by 16 September. There is also cooked rice, but nobody labelled when it was made. Five people need dinner. Room 2 requested a vegetarian meal and said eggs and dairy are acceptable. Room 4 wrote “possibly allergic to shellfish” on the booking form but did not mention ordinary fish; this has not been confirmed with them. The pantry has vegetable stock, tinned lentils, pasta, oats, mustard and dried herbs. No shopping delivery is available tonight. The oven works, but the large hob ring is awaiting repair.
instance.deliverable: A concise cook-facing summary of usable ingredients, dietary needs, equipment limits, and items requiring exclusion or clarification.
instance.answer_conditions: The summary must identify five diners, the vegetarian requirement, the unconfirmed Room 4 allergy note, the broken large hob ring, and the available ingredients. It should flag the haddock as past its use-by date and the rice as undated rather than recommending either, without inventing a menu or declaring ordinary fish safe for Room 4.

instance.task_summary: Combine several volunteers’ book-club ideas into a coherent committee brief that distinguishes agreed features from unresolved choices while protecting confidentiality.
givens: The requester explains at length that three volunteers sent overlapping and sometimes contradictory ideas, and she has been asked to turn them into something the Village Library Committee can actually discuss.
She wants a 180-word brief for the committee’s 24 September meeting so it can approve a three-month pilot rather than revisit every comment.
Because she knows several contributors through her GP reception work, she is particularly concerned that no patient anecdote or identifiable health detail should survive into the brief.

constraints.text: Keep the committee brief to no more than 180 words.
Use one section for common ground and another for unresolved choices.
Omit names and the health anecdote; retain only a general accessibility rationale if relevant.
Reconcile the notes without implying that disputed points have been settled.

instance.packet: Maya proposes a monthly book club on the second Thursday at 6:30 p.m., beginning 12 October, with meetings lasting 75 minutes. She suggests alternating novels and memoirs and limiting attendance to 14 so everyone can speak. Tom prefers weekly meetings, no attendance cap and only books already held by the library. Both want tea, large-print copies where possible and a three-month trial. Leanne suggests charging £3 per meeting for refreshments; Maya thinks the library should seek a small grant and keep attendance free. Tom says participants could bring their own drinks. Everyone agrees that the first title should be under 300 pages and available as an audiobook. Suggested titles are The Thursday Murder Club, Small Things Like These and Foster. Maya mentioned by name a surgery patient with depression who found a reading group helpful. The library manager has offered the upstairs meeting room free of charge, but it seats only 12 and has no lift. The accessible ground-floor room seats 18 but costs £20 per evening. Publicity could begin on 25 September if the committee agrees the schedule, fee and room.
instance.deliverable: A privacy-safe, coherent committee brief summarizing common ground and clearly listing the schedule, fee, room, capacity, and first-title decisions still required.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must preserve the agreed three-month trial, refreshments, large-print preference, under-300-page first title, and audiobook availability. It must present frequency, attendance cap, fee, room accessibility/cost, and title as unresolved. It must omit all names and the patient’s condition, stay within 180 words, and use the requested two-part structure.

instance.task_summary: Summarize a pet-behaviour course renewal notice for the requester’s son so they can decide whether cancellation or a refund request is worth pursuing.
givens: The requester says she joined the course after adopting an anxious greyhound but has barely used it because the laptop text is difficult for her to read.
She wants a clear summary for her son, who checks her card statements, focusing on the charge, deadlines, usage record, cancellation route, and whether access ends immediately.
She asks for short headings and a maximum of 140 words.

constraints.text: Keep the summary to no more than 140 words.
Organize the summary with brief descriptive headings.
Distinguish the general refund policy from the actual account usage and do not promise that a refund will be granted.

instance.packet: Happy Hound Signals membership notice. Your annual membership renewed automatically on 12 September 2026 for AUD 119.00 using the Visa card ending 2841. Renewal reminders were emailed on 13 August and 5 September. Annual memberships may be cancelled at any time through Account Settings. Cancellation stops the next renewal but access continues until the current paid term ends. A refund may be requested within 14 calendar days of renewal if no more than three course lessons have been completed during the renewed term. Requests must be sent through the billing form by 11:59 p.m. AEST on 26 September 2026. Approval is subject to an account review and normally takes five business days. The account activity report shows 3 of 24 lessons opened since renewal: “Lip Licking and Yawning,” “When a Dog Freezes,” and “Creating a Quiet Retreat.” Each is marked 20% complete. Captions and downloadable large-print transcripts are available from the accessibility menu. Turning off auto-renewal does not itself submit a refund request.
instance.deliverable: A headed summary for the requester’s son covering the renewal, apparent refund eligibility, deadline, cancellation effect, and accessibility options.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must say that the membership renewed for AUD 119.00 on 12 September 2026, that the account is exactly at the three-lesson policy limit, and that a refund may be requested by 11:59 p.m. AEST on 26 September but is not guaranteed. It must clarify that cancellation only prevents the next renewal, current access continues, and a separate billing form is required. It should mention the large-print transcripts and remain within 140 words.

instance.task_summary: Summarize a Mediterranean wildfire ecology article for a ferry deckhand and his photography group, defining pyrodiversity while distinguishing beneficial fire variation from destructive extreme fires.
givens: The requester is a 55-year-old Orkney ferry deckhand who photographs seabirds and has no ecology training.
He encountered a headline suggesting that varied fires can benefit wildlife, while another report described all wildfires as ecological disasters.
The summary is intended for the requester and his deck crew photo group so they can understand and discuss the apparent contradiction.

constraints.text: Keep the summary to no more than 130 words.
Define pyrodiversity first, distinguish periodic varied fire from frequent severe fire, and retain the source's warning that benefits are context-dependent.
Use language understandable without ecological training.

instance.packet:
Headline: Why “pyrodiversity” can help Mediterranean wildlife

Pyrodiversity means variation in the timing, size, intensity and frequency of fires across a landscape. In some Mediterranean ecosystems, occasional fires of different kinds create a patchwork: recently burned ground, recovering scrub and older woodland. That mixture can provide feeding or nesting opportunities for different species and prevent every area from reaching the same stage at once.

This does not mean that more fire is automatically better. Large, fast-moving fires during extreme heat can kill wildlife, strip soil and overwhelm plants’ ability to recover. Repeated burning at short intervals may stop shrubs and trees from reaching maturity. By contrast, carefully managed low-intensity burns may reduce fuel in selected places, but they are not suitable everywhere.

Researchers therefore treat pyrodiversity as a context-dependent idea, not a universal rule. Its effects vary with habitat, species, weather, grazing and previous fires. Longer droughts and accumulated vegetation can also turn a historically tolerable fire regime into a destructive one.
instance.deliverable: A plain-English summary of no more than 130 words for the requester and his deck crew photo group.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must accurately define pyrodiversity, reconcile the apparently conflicting claims, preserve the source's context-dependent caveat, avoid implying that wildfires are generally beneficial, and remain within 130 words.

instance.task_summary: Summarize a recipe-service renewal notice for a retired subscriber and her daughter so they can understand the charge, refund conditions, and cancellation deadline.
givens: The requester was charged £59.99 for a CookVault subscription on 12 September 2026 and says she barely uses it.
She wants a clear summary for herself and her adult daughter before they decide whether to request a refund.

constraints.text: Organize the summary under “Charge,” “Refund,” and “Next step.”
State the exact cancellation deadline and the activity that would make the account ineligible under the supplied policy.
Explain the notice without subscription or legal jargon.

instance.packet:
CookVault Annual Plus renewal notice — 12 September 2026

Your Annual Plus membership renewed today for £59.99 using the card ending 1842. The new membership period runs from 12 September 2026 to 11 September 2027. Switching off automatic renewal prevents another charge next year but does not cancel or refund this renewal.

Our voluntary renewal policy allows you to request cancellation within 14 days of the renewal date, up to and including 26 September 2026. A full refund is available only if, after renewal, no premium recipe has been downloaded and no weekly meal plan has been exported. Merely opening the app or viewing a recipe does not affect eligibility.

Refund requests must be submitted through Account > Membership > Request a refund. Approved refunds return to the original payment card within 5–10 working days. If the online form is inaccessible, telephone 020 7946 0188 between 09:00 and 17:00, Monday to Friday.
instance.deliverable: A three-part plain-English summary for the subscriber and her daughter to use when deciding whether to seek a refund.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must identify the charged amount and membership period, distinguish disabling auto-renewal from refunding the current renewal, state the 26 September deadline, explain the download/export exclusion accurately, and give the correct request route.

instance.task_summary: Summarize family dietary replies for an anniversary caterer.
givens: The requester asks: “Summarise these dietary replies so our anniversary caterer can plan.”
instance.packet:
Family WhatsApp replies, 14 September:

Asha: I do not eat meat, but fish and eggs are fine.

Ben: I have coeliac disease, so my food must be gluten-free and protected from crumbs or shared utensils.

Maya: I have a severe sesame allergy and carry an adrenaline pen. Please check sauces, bread and garnishes as well as the main dish.

Tom: I eat meat, but ordinary milk and cream upset my stomach; lactose-free dairy is fine.
