instance.task_summary: Summarize a customs-guidance subscription renewal notice for the requester's daughter so she can assess refund eligibility and understand which parcel-declaration features would be lost.
givens: The requester is an 82-year-old retired shopkeeper in Leicester who speaks Gujarati at home and is compiling family recipes for his great-grandchildren.
He subscribed to CustomsMate Plus for occasional overseas parcels containing printed family recipes and permitted packaged ingredients, but has used it only once.
He wants the summary for his daughter Nisha, who manages his online accounts, so she can decide whether to seek a refund.
He says that no Plus feature has been used since the latest renewal.

constraints.text: Use the headings “Renewal and refund” and “Customs-declaration access”.
State the apparent refund position and identify what Nisha should verify before submitting the request.
Use clear, non-technical language suitable for reading aloud to the requester.

instance.packet:
Subject: Your CustomsMate Plus subscription has renewed

On 14 September 2026, we charged £39.99 to the Visa card ending 1842 for another year of CustomsMate Plus. Invoice: CM-88417. Your new term ends on 13 September 2027.

You may cancel renewal at any time. For a full refund of this year’s charge, submit the refund form by 28 September 2026 and confirm that, since renewal, you have not generated a shipping label, saved a CN22 or CN23 form, or contacted a customs adviser. Merely opening an article does not count as using a paid feature. An approved refund ends Plus access immediately.

The free plan retains the customs glossary and sample declarations. Plus adds guided CN22/CN23 prompts, saved parcel records, printable packing checklists and destination-specific restricted-goods alerts. CustomsMate does not file declarations or guarantee that a parcel will be accepted. The sender remains responsible for checking the destination country’s current rules.

Refund requests must quote the invoice number and be sent through the account support form.
instance.deliverable: A concise, two-section summary for Nisha covering the charge, deadline, apparent refund eligibility, required checks, and the customs-declaration features retained or lost.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must explain that a full refund appears available if the form is submitted by 28 September 2026 and no listed paid feature has been used since renewal; opening an article does not disqualify him. It must tell Nisha to verify account activity and quote CM-88417. It must distinguish the free glossary and samples from the Plus prompts, saved records, checklists, and alerts, and note that the service neither files declarations nor guarantees parcel acceptance. It should not invent cancellation steps, shipping permissions, or legal assurances beyond the notice.

instance.task_summary: Prove at secondary-school level that the median of three ordered weekday deadlines uniquely minimizes the total absolute distance to them.
givens: The weekdays are encoded as integers from Monday = 1 through Sunday = 7.
The three deadline days satisfy a≤b≤c.
The candidate day x belongs to {1,…,7}.
The objective is |x−a|+|x−b|+|x−c|.

constraints.text: Use reasoning accessible at secondary-school level.
Prove both minimality and uniqueness, not merely that x=b attains some value.

instance.deliverable: A secondary-school-level proof that the objective is minimized uniquely at x=b.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must prove the claim for all ordered a,b,c in {1,…,7}. A valid argument may compare the objective on the intervals x≤a, a≤x≤b, b≤x≤c, and x≥c, showing it strictly decreases up to b and strictly increases after b. It must explicitly establish uniqueness, including cases where two or all deadlines coincide.

instance.task_summary: Determine whether formatting a dashcam’s microSD card is sufficient preparation before giving the camera away.

instance.task_summary: Create a staged plan for assembling an accessible residency-evidence file, checking coverage across ten six-month periods, and identifying gaps before the deadline.
givens: The applicant is an 84-year-old retired music teacher in Christchurch who still accompanies a community choir.
She needs to assemble proof of residence covering 1 July 2021 to 30 June 2026 for an application due on 2 October 2026.
Her available resources are her passport, five annual IRD income summaries, two tenancy agreements, power bills, community-choir engagement letters, a home scanner, and twelve labelled paper folders.
She wants to inventory the documents first, map them against each six-month period, and then prepare a list of gaps requiring replacement records.

constraints.text: The complete evidence file and gap list must be ready by 2 October 2026.

constraints.params: one dated document per six-month period from 1 July 2021 to 30 June 2026
constraints.text: The plan must check for at least one dated document in each of the ten consecutive six-month periods.
All labels, checklists, and the gap list must use high-contrast formatting and text of at least 18-point.
No sorting or scanning session may last longer than 45 minutes.
Original documents must remain in their labelled paper folders; only scans or copies may be placed in the application set.

instance.deliverable: A dated, step-by-step preparation plan with sessions of no more than 45 minutes, a ten-period coverage checklist, a document-to-period filing method, and a final gap list.
instance.answer_conditions: The response must sequence inventory, coverage checking, scanning, and gap follow-up; correctly divide the five-year span into ten consecutive six-month periods without gaps or overlaps; respect the deadline, accessibility requirement, session cap, and preservation of originals; and avoid claiming that any listed document is officially sufficient unless the issuing authority has confirmed it.
